# Phase One — Broad Movie Possibility Space

From one point of intent let many frames arise; the Awtsmoos gives every vessel a different disguise.
The protocol should describe meaning, not dictate renderer internals, so 2D and 3D can share time without sharing every implementation.

## Movie Language Possibilities
- Narrative films: casts, dialogue beats, blocking, gaze, expression, entrances, exits, reactions.
- Tutorials: numbered steps, cursor/hand focus, arrows, highlights, zooms, labels, callouts, before/after states.
- Infographics: bar, line, pie/donut, counters, timelines, progress rings, maps-as-shapes, comparison cards.
- Motion graphics: text, rectangles, circles, polygons, paths, patches, masks, gradients, strokes, icons, grids.
- 3D scenes: cameras, perspective, lights, world objects, character/object transforms, fog/depth declarations.
- Particles: sparks, snow, dust, confetti, fireflies, trails, bursts, star fields, data points.
- Cinematography: wide, medium, closeup, extreme closeup, overhead, low/high angle, POV, orbit, dolly, truck, crane, rack-focus intent.
- Transitions: cut, crossfade, wipe, push, zoom, iris, match-motion, dip, flash.
- Animation: keyframes, easing, spring intent, loops, staggering, path motion, transform/opacity/style channels.
- Audio metadata: dialogue/music/SFX cues and ducking intent, even when a renderer only preserves metadata.
- Accessibility: safe title areas, caption semantics, contrast hints, reduced-motion substitutions.
- Formats: landscape, portrait, square, responsive preview, explicit FPS/duration.

## Five Candidate Architectures
### A — One Giant Renderer
One engine draws everything. Rejected: destroys mature app identities and duplicates specialist work.

### B — Shared JSON Protocol + Capability Adapters
Canonical movie document plus per-app adapters. Preferred: AI gets one language while each app advertises supported subsets.

### C — Nesher as Universal Host
Everything becomes NLE clips. Useful for finishing, weak for semantic authoring and live procedural character control.

### D — Animator as Universal Host
Everything becomes Animator entities. Strong cinematic path, but over-couples simple motion graphics and editing workflows.

### E — Event Bus Only
Apps exchange loose events. Flexible but insufficiently deterministic for AI generation, validation, or durable movie files.

## Preferred Direction
Architecture B, with optional handoff into D for cinematic realization and C for finishing/export. Captions remains a fast 2D composition pet; Animator remains the director/world pet; Nesher remains the editor/export pet.

## Ideal End State
An AI can inspect `capabilities()`, emit one schema-valid document, preview it, hand scenes to the best renderer, preserve unsupported semantic layers for another app, and export or edit without reverse-engineering private internals.
